summary.headline: Saturn and Jupiter Configurations
summary.text: Astrological doctrine on the configurations of the stars, attributed to Maser the Persian and Muhamates the Balkhian and translated from Persian. It interprets Saturn–Jupiter and Saturn–Mars configurations—conjunction, sextile, trine, square, opposition, and house positions—as omens of destruction, war, sedition, religious corruption, famine, prosperity, and political events, with a note that Achmes borrowed from Ptolemy’s Tetrabiblos.
